claims.text: The starting alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
Diffusion-based surface aluminization will produce an aluminum-enriched near-surface region on HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminum in the near-surface region will react with oxygen to form an Al2O3 scale.
The resulting alumina scale will be thin, continuous, adherent, and thermodynamically stable.
The alumina scale will inhibit oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C.
Inhibiting oxygen ingress will reduce high-temperature oxidation, weight gain, and surface degradation relative to untreated HfNbTaTiZr.
Restricting aluminization to the surface will leave the alloy's bulk microstructure substantially unchanged.
The as-cast bulk microstructure is responsible for the alloy's useful mechanical properties.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, the alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, the alloy will retain a high-temperature yield strength within 163–530 MPa.
The proposed protection is intended to remain effective during mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed treatment is intended to protect the alloy in an oxygen-rich atmosphere at approximately 1000 °C for tens to hundreds of hours.
Prolonged high-temperature processing could alter an as-cast high-entropy-alloy microstructure.
Excessive aluminide diffusion could degrade HfNbTaTiZr or alter its as-cast microstructure.
